commit_message:
[Runtime][WASM] Handle wasm64 pointers in JS completion drains (#25054)

Completion-buffer pointers arrive in JavaScript as BigInts, but
Int32Array expects a numeric byte offset. Passing the pointer directly
throws `TypeError: Cannot convert a BigInt value to a number`.

This converts wasm64 pointers before accessing memory and keeps wasm32
pointers unsigned in the inline and shared-ring completion paths.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: issue-greeter

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Require output channel reuse for im2col

The im2col control function rejected only convolutions without an
output channel loop, so a depthwise convolution with a unit channel
multiplier, whose output channel loop has extent one, was still
rewritten even though nothing reuses its gathered input. Require an
output channel loop whose extent is not statically one; a dynamic
extent may exceed one and counts as reuse.

Pass the already inferred convolution dimensions to the control
function, so selection uses the same dimensions as the rewrite instead
of inferring them again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

The im2col control function rejected only convolutions without an
output channel loop, so a depthwise convolution with a unit channel
multiplier, whose output channel loop has extent one, was still
rewritten even though nothing reuses its gathered input. Require an
output channel loop whose extent is not statically one; a dynamic
extent may exceed one and counts as reuse.

Pass the already inferred convolution dimensions to the control
function, so selection uses the same dimensions as the rewrite instead
of inferring them again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: runtime :: macos-15

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Require output channel reuse for im2col

The im2col control function rejected only convolutions without an
output channel loop, so a depthwise convolution with a unit channel
multiplier, whose output channel loop has extent one, was still
rewritten even though nothing reuses its gathered input. Require an
output channel loop whose extent is not statically one; a dynamic
extent may exceed one and counts as reuse.

Pass the already inferred convolution dimensions to the control
function, so selection uses the same dimensions as the rewrite instead
of inferring them again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Runtime][WASM] Handle wasm64 pointers in JS completion drains (#25054)

Completion-buffer pointers arrive in JavaScript as BigInts, but
Int32Array expects a numeric byte offset. Passing the pointer directly
throws `TypeError: Cannot convert a BigInt value to a number`.

This converts wasm64 pointers before accessing memory and keeps wasm32
pointers unsigned in the inline and shared-ring completion paths.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: issue-greeter

commit_message:
[Runtime][WASM] Handle wasm64 pointers in JS completion drains (#25054)

Completion-buffer pointers arrive in JavaScript as BigInts, but
Int32Array expects a numeric byte offset. Passing the pointer directly
throws `TypeError: Cannot convert a BigInt value to a number`.

This converts wasm64 pointers before accessing memory and keeps wasm32
pointers unsigned in the inline and shared-ring completion paths.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: linux_x64_gcc

commit_message:
[Runtime][WASM] Handle wasm64 pointers in JS completion drains (#25054)

Completion-buffer pointers arrive in JavaScript as BigInts, but
Int32Array expects a numeric byte offset. Passing the pointer directly
throws `TypeError: Cannot convert a BigInt value to a number`.

This converts wasm64 pointers before accessing memory and keeps wasm32
pointers unsigned in the inline and shared-ring completion paths.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Runtime][WASM] Handle wasm64 pointers in JS completion drains (#25054)

Completion-buffer pointers arrive in JavaScript as BigInts, but
Int32Array expects a numeric byte offset. Passing the pointer directly
throws `TypeError: Cannot convert a BigInt value to a number`.

This converts wasm64 pointers before accessing memory and keeps wasm32
pointers unsigned in the inline and shared-ring completion paths.

Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@6be022066fd2 (#25045)

Adapted to change of ROCDL "wave per eu" attributes type from int to
string in LLVM commit 4d5db577f969 [mlir][ROCDL][AMDGPU] Support string
waves_per_eu for min,max occupancy range (#225663)

The TOSA compliance table has grown beyond what MSVC can support on the
stack.
Apparently, the function size / stack size has been an issue before, see
e.g.:
9e69e851a1f8 [NFC][mlir][tosa] Use optnone for compliance initialization
under ASan (#229292)
1e9bc138d8f3 [mlir][Tosa] Optimize compliance initialization for size to
improve build time (NFC) (#222791)
This change currently adds an experimental mitigation to the LLVM fork
by splitting up the initialization.
    
Claude Code has been used to find the LLVM commits related to the issued
and adapt the IREE side code. The changes have been reviewed manually.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[WebGPU] Retain builtin buffers until submission (#25068)

The builtin fill and unaligned-copy paths destroy their parameter
buffers before submitting the recorded commands. WebGPU then rejects the
submission with `Buffer used in submit while destroyed`.

This keeps those buffers alive until submission and cleans them up on
both success and error paths. I've checked direct execution and recorded
command replay in Chrome/WebGPU.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>

The builtin fill and unaligned-copy paths destroy their parameter
buffers before submitting the recorded commands. WebGPU then rejects the
submission with `Buffer used in submit while destroyed`.

This keeps those buffers alive until submission and cleans them up on
both success and error paths. I've checked direct execution and recorded
command replay in Chrome/WebGPU.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: runtime_tracing :: ubuntu-24.04-arm :: console

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Make im2col a generic convolution rewrite (#25011)

Replaces the three layout-specific im2col patterns (NHWC, NCHW,
depthwise NHWC) with one generic rewrite that handles any convolution,
named or generic, including grouped, dilated, 1-D/3-D, dynamic and
integer ones.

The pattern gathers the convolved input with an all-parallel
`linalg.generic`, rewires the op to read the gather, keeps the original
payload, and collapses the result into a matmul using
`DispatchCreation::getCollapsibleLoops`. Add a basic heuristic via a
control function that skips convolutions without an output channel
dimension (depthwise, pooling), where the gather is never amortized.

The pass is renamed to `iree-global-opt-convert-conv-to-im2col`; the
pipeline flag is unchanged.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Expand QDQ contractions over collapsed operands

The Torch frontend dequantizes blockwise operands as [M, G, L] and
[N, G, L] and collapses them back into K before the matmul, with the
weight also transposed for a linear layer. The collapse_shape hid the
dequantize from ConvertQDQToIntegerMath, so the matmul stayed in
floating point.

PropagateAffineQuantization now reuses the upstream
reshape-by-expansion patterns, gated to a collapse_shape of a
dequantize consumed by a linalg.transpose or by a contraction whose
inputs are all dequantized. The transpose moves the collapse_shape
after itself and folds into the dequantize. The contraction expands to
iterate over (m, n, g, l), and the expand_shapes added to its other
inputs cancel their collapse_shapes. The integer rewrite then reduces
each block in i32 and the blocks in floating point.

Fixes #25085

[GlobalOptimization] Expand QDQ contractions over collapsed operands

The Torch frontend dequantizes blockwise operands as [M, G, L] and
[N, G, L] and collapses them back into K before the matmul, with the
weight also transposed for a linear layer. The collapse_shape hid the
dequantize from ConvertQDQToIntegerMath, so the matmul stayed in
floating point.

PropagateAffineQuantization now reuses the upstream
reshape-by-expansion patterns, gated to a collapse_shape of a
dequantize consumed by a linalg.transpose or by a contraction whose
inputs are all dequantized. The transpose moves the collapse_shape
after itself and folds into the dequantize. The contraction expands to
iterate over (m, n, g, l), and the expand_shapes added to its other
inputs cancel their collapse_shapes. The integer rewrite then reduces
each block in i32 and the blocks in floating point.

Fixes #25085

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Expand QDQ contractions over collapsed operands

The Torch frontend dequantizes blockwise operands as [M, G, L] and
[N, G, L] and collapses them back into K before the matmul, with the
weight also transposed for a linear layer. The collapse_shape hid the
dequantize from ConvertQDQToIntegerMath, so the matmul stayed in
floating point.

PropagateAffineQuantization now reuses the upstream
reshape-by-expansion patterns, gated to a collapse_shape of a
dequantize consumed by a linalg.transpose or by a contraction whose
inputs are all dequantized. The transpose moves the collapse_shape
after itself and folds into the dequantize. The contraction expands to
iterate over (m, n, g, l), and the expand_shapes added to its other
inputs cancel their collapse_shapes. The integer rewrite then reduces
each block in i32 and the blocks in floating point.

Fixes #25085

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Make im2col a generic convolution rewrite (#25011)

Replaces the three layout-specific im2col patterns (NHWC, NCHW,
depthwise NHWC) with one generic rewrite that handles any convolution,
named or generic, including grouped, dilated, 1-D/3-D, dynamic and
integer ones.

The pattern gathers the convolved input with an all-parallel
`linalg.generic`, rewires the op to read the gather, keeps the original
payload, and collapses the result into a matmul using
`DispatchCreation::getCollapsibleLoops`. Add a basic heuristic via a
control function that skips convolutions without an output channel
dimension (depthwise, pooling), where the gather is never amortized.

The pass is renamed to `iree-global-opt-convert-conv-to-im2col`; the
pipeline flag is unchanged.

commit_message:
[Runtime][WASM] Handle wasm64 pointers in JS completion drains (#25054)

Completion-buffer pointers arrive in JavaScript as BigInts, but
Int32Array expects a numeric byte offset. Passing the pointer directly
throws `TypeError: Cannot convert a BigInt value to a number`.

This converts wasm64 pointers before accessing memory and keeps wasm32
pointers unsigned in the inline and shared-ring completion paths.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: issue-greeter

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Require output channel reuse for im2col

The im2col control function rejected only convolutions without an
output channel loop, so a depthwise convolution with a unit channel
multiplier, whose output channel loop has extent one, was still
rewritten even though nothing reuses its gathered input. Require an
output channel loop whose extent is not statically one; a dynamic
extent may exceed one and counts as reuse.

Pass the already inferred convolution dimensions to the control
function, so selection uses the same dimensions as the rewrite instead
of inferring them again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
